quarterly_data.signal: Q4 and full-year 2025 headline results (CEO Dara Khosrowshahi): trips on the platform accelerated again to a 15 billion annual run rate and audience grew to more than 200 million monthly active users, driving Q4 gross bookings up 22% year-on-year; 2025 was the fifth consecutive year of annual gross bookings growth over 20%, with $8.7 billion in adjusted EBITDA (up 35%) and $9.8 billion in free cash flow (up 42%).
quarterly_data.figure: 15 billion annual run rate; more than 200 million monthly active users; gross bookings up 22% year-on-year; $8.7 billion in adjusted EBITDA, up 35%; $9.8 billion in free cash flow, up 42%

quarterly_data.signal: AV positioning and economics (CEO): after multiple AV deployments worldwide, 'we're more convinced than ever that AVs will unlock a multitrillion-dollar opportunity for Uber'; AVs are acting as a net growth driver where they operate (San Francisco, Austin and Atlanta gross bookings accelerated); AVs on Uber's platform run at significantly higher utilization than 1P stand-alone platforms, with trips per vehicle per day 30% higher based on publicly available data, and better ETAs; new AV products launch at lower margins that improve over time, and the at-scale deals being struck now with AV partners carry 'good positive margins' based on current consumer fares.
quarterly_data.figure: multitrillion-dollar opportunity; trips per vehicle per day are 30% higher

quarterly_data.signal: AV rollout target and launch requirements (CEO): with partnerships including Waymo, NVIDIA, Waabi, Avride and Nuro/Lucid (which has a production-ready car), Uber expects to be in 15 cities by the end of this year and to expand beyond that; each city launch needs a partner deal, capital for the vehicles, depots and real estate, charging infrastructure, regulator readiness and a safety case with the partner - launches usually start with a driver in the vehicle, who is later taken out, as Uber has done in Abu Dhabi.
quarterly_data.figure: 15 cities by the end of this year

quarterly_data.signal: AV capital deployment to guarantee supply (CEO and incoming CFO Balaji Krishnamurthy): Uber is investing in AV software players - its latest investment, in Waabi (a leading AV trucking provider moving into passenger mobility), makes the first 25,000 passenger vehicles produced on Waabi's platform exclusive on Uber; more such commitments will follow (Nuro, Lucid and others), much of that supply on profitable economics; Uber is talking to financial institutions, private equity players and banks about fleet financing for AVs and EVs, expecting the ecosystem to financialize like hotels and data centers; with 'tens of thousands of vehicles already announced in a few partnerships', Uber expects those commitments to be financialized over time but will step in with some vehicle purchases in the first few years.
quarterly_data.figure: first 25,000 passenger vehicles exclusive on Uber; tens of thousands of vehicles already announced in a few partnerships

quarterly_data.signal: AV scaling stages and bottleneck (incoming CFO Balaji Krishnamurthy): stage one is launching in multiple markets with AVs as baseload supply at the demand trough - in the Austin deployment AV demand is much more consistent than the network's Saturday-to-Monday drop of about 45%; the next stage requires the vehicle platform cost to come down so consumer prices can fall and the TAM expands; getting to tens of thousands of vehicles 'will come down to how quickly OEMs can ramp production', so OEMs need to start ramping capacity now, with offtake commitments and asset financialization playing a big role.
quarterly_data.figure: Saturday to Monday drop for our network, which is about 45%

quarterly_data.signal: AV supplier landscape (CEO): AV will not become winner-take-most because hardware is different - OEM manufacturing is local, and the CEO's vision is that 10 years from now every new car sold will have full L3/L4 software attached, so there will be many suppliers; multiple players are getting to the finish line (Waymo; Pony, WeRide and Baidu in China, with Uber partnering outside the U.S.; Waabi, Wayve, Nuro and Avride), and NVIDIA is developing a hardware platform, sensor stack and compute stack that Uber believes will be the industry standard, and is now also building full self-driving software; Uber positions itself as the winner-take-most 3P marketplace.

AV disruption exposure (incoming CFO and CEO): answering whether AV ramps in major cities threaten share and profits, incoming CFO Balaji Krishnamurthy said '70% of the U.S. is outside of the stock markets' (as transcribed; he was responding about the top markets) and nearly 75% of Uber's U.S. profits come from those markets, which are growing faster than the top 20 cities; those non-top 20 markets are unlikely to be addressed by AVs for a long time to come. The CEO added that 60% of mobility gross bookings are international, outside of the U.S.
quarterly_data.figure: 70% of the U.S.; nearly 75% of our U.S. profits; 60% of our mobility gross bookings are international

quarterly_data.signal: Audience and 2026 growth drivers (incoming CFO and CEO): MAPC growth stepped up from about 14% year-on-year at the start of 2025 to 18% at year-end, with over 202 million monthly actives and an annual active base over 450 million; 40% of consumers in Q4 were using more than one Uber product; the CEO said membership has 46 million members, growing faster than 50%, and the incoming CFO said the membership program is growing 55% year-on-year; in the U.S., insurance reform and product-driven hundreds of millions of dollars of cost savings are turning insurance from a deleveraging cost into leverage, letting Uber hold prices flat or better, which supports an accelerating U.S. core business.
quarterly_data.figure: MAPC growth at about 14% year-on-year (start of 2025) and 18% year-on-year (end of 2025); over 202 million monthly actives; annual active base is over 450 million; 40% of consumers in Q4 were using more than one Uber product; 46 million members, growing faster than 50%; membership program growing 55% year-on-year
